evergreen_facts.text: The Romans founded Londinium on the River Thames around AD 47, the beginning of London.
The Great Fire of London in 1666 burned for days and destroyed most of the medieval City of London.
The world's first underground railway, the Metropolitan Railway, opened in London in 1863.
The Tower of London was founded by William the Conqueror after the Norman conquest of 1066.
London's St Paul's Cathedral, with its great dome, was designed by Christopher Wren after the Great Fire.
Westminster Abbey in London has been the coronation church of English and British monarchs since 1066.
Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell in the clock tower of London's Palace of Westminster.
The River Thames winds through the middle of London on its way east to the North Sea.
The Prime Meridian, the line of zero degrees longitude, runs through the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London.
Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 in his laboratory at St Mary's Hospital in London.
Shakespeare's Globe on London's South Bank is a reconstruction of the open-air playhouse of Shakespeare's time.
The British Museum in London, founded in 1753, holds the Rosetta Stone among millions of objects.
Fish and chips became a popular takeaway in London and northern England in the second half of the 1800s.
Pie and mash with a green parsley sauce called liquor is a traditional working-class meal of East London.
Wimbledon, played in southwest London since 1877, is the oldest tennis tournament in the world.
London has hosted the Summer Olympics three times, in 1908, 1948 and 2012.
